content: 1. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. When initiating riociguat in patients receiving atazanavir, start with a dose of 5 mg three times daily. Monitor for signs and symptoms of hypotension during initiation and treatment. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), which may elevate the risk of adverse reactions. 4. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both atazanavir and ritonavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Close monitoring is required. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is still recommended. 6. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. 9. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Atazanavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 11. Atazanavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. There is a potential for increased toxicity. Alternatives should be used if available. Limit the rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg/day. The ritonavir component of the atazanavir/ritonavir regimen decreases rosuvastatin metabolism. 12. Atazanavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. There is a potential for increased toxicity, including an elevated risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 13. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 14. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 15. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily in patients with a platelet count of ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily in patients with a platelet count of ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 17. Atazanavir increases the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. There is a potential for increased toxicity and systemic effects. 18. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Atazanavir increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 20. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If use is unavoidable, reduce the selpercatinib dose as per its prescribing information. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, wait at least 3 to 5 half-lives of the discontinued drug before resuming the original selpercatinib dose. 21. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its monograph. After discontinuation of the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives, resume the original selumetinib dose. 22. Atazanavir increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. There is a potential for increased toxicity. 23. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Never use sildenafil chronically for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with atazanavir. 24. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to an increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. 26. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. 27. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Atazanavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 29. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 32. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If use is unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 37. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 38. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 39. Stiripentol affects atazanavir levels by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 40. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 41. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 42. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Atazanavir increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Atazanavir increases the levels of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Stop tadalafil >24 hours before protease inhibitor (PI) initiation, restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 46. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases the metabolism of tamoxifen to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biological activity. 47. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. There is a potential for increased toxicity. 48. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of tazemetostat with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 50. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. 51. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Atazanavir increases the levels of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. There is a potential for increased toxicity. 53. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels of atazanavir by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both atazanavir and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 54. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 55. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 57. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Atazanavir increases the levels of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 60. Atazanavir increases the effects of timolol through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval.
